summary: Tested the Notification Inbox feature. Backend: all 4 /api/notifications endpoints work. Each one returns 401 without a token. The list shows only the caller's own alerts, newest first, with no _id. Marking another user's alert, or a bad id, as read returns 404. Read-all only affects the caller. Alerts are created by the background task when: an admin posts news, an event or a notice (every user except the posting admin; links /news, /events, /events?tab=1); an admin approves or rejects an entry (sent to the owner; the reject reason is included; links /detail/{id}); a user submits an entry or a complaint (sent to admins; links /detail/{id} and /admin). Frontend: inbox_user saw the bell badge (10). Tapping the bell opened the list with 10 items and unread dots. Tapping a notice opened /events?tab=1 on the Notice Board tab. Tapping a news alert opened /news and marked it read (8 unread after). Read-all cleared every dot and hid the Read all button. The dashboard badge disappeared on return. Read state carried over between sessions. A fresh signup sees the empty state (notifications-empty) and no badge. Admin alerts open the detail screen and the Admin Panel. Regression passed: dashboard cards, the News terms dialog, the More sheet (Complaints), and the profile sheet (My Submissions, Logout). No deprecated Expo packages detected.

minor.issue: asyncio.create_task(...) result is not kept anywhere. Python only weakly references pending tasks, so a fan-out can be garbage-collected mid-run. Store the task in a module-level set and remove it with add_done_callback, or use FastAPI BackgroundTasks.
Deleting a post leaves its inbox alerts in place. Tapping one opens the list screen and the item is gone. Optionally delete alerts by post or tag them with a ref_id.
Capped at 200 with no pagination, while unread-count counts everything. A user with more than 200 alerts can see a badge for items they cannot reach. There is no retention or cleanup.

integration_issues.issue: Opens the Admin Panel on the Pending tab, not the Complaints tab. The admin has to tap Complaints by hand. Consider action_url '/admin?tab=complaints' with matching param handling in admin.tsx.

issues: Alerts titled 'New submission' fall back to the generic bell-outline icon (iconFor only matches /news, /events, /admin and Approved/Not approved titles). A dedicated icon such as clipboard-plus would read better.

action_items: Keep a reference to the fire-and-forget tasks in notify() so they cannot be garbage-collected.
Optional: deep-link complaint alerts to the Admin > Complaints tab.
Optional: give 'New submission' alerts their own icon; consider pagination or retention for notifications.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:188: the task from asyncio.create_task is not retained.

notifications.tsx:44: the per-item read POST is fire-and-forget with an empty catch. If it fails, the UI shows the alert as read while the server still counts it unread. The dashboard badge re-syncs on focus.
The test DB now holds TEST_ alerts for inbox_user and admin from the test runs (cleaned-up posts left alerts behind).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Stacked screens stay in the DOM on Expo web. Use the :visible selector, e.g. '[data-testid="header-back-button"]:visible'. Run pytest with -n 0 (pytest.ini sets xdist) and EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (the frontend .env uses EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL, not EXPO_BACKEND_URL). Push returns 401 from the relay because the key is a placeholder; this is expected.
